request:
Our campus has a lost-and-found desk and we want a simple board for it. Anyone who finds something can report it with a short description of the item, where they found it and the date they found it. People should be able to see all the items on the board and look at one item. When the owner comes to collect an item, the desk marks it as claimed and writes down the owner's name. An item that has already been claimed cannot be claimed again. We also want to see only the items that are still waiting for their owners.

The client's answers to your questions:
Q: Should only desk staff be able to mark an item as claimed (needing some kind of login or password), or can anyone using the board do it?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: When people look at a claimed item, should the owner's name be shown to everyone, or kept visible only to the desk?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: Should items ever be removed from the board, for example after they are claimed or after a set number of days unclaimed? If so, how long?
A: No, they stay on the full list, but the list of waiting items should only show unclaimed ones.

Where the client has no preference or did not answer, choose the simplest option and add nothing they did not ask for (no logins, PINs or extra required fields).
summary:
I've built the lost-and-found board in `app.py`. All 11 of my tests pass. Items are saved in a file called `lost_and_found.db` in the project folder.

**Endpoints:**
- **`POST /items`**: report a found item. You send a `description`, a `location` and a `found_date` (written like `2024-05-01`). It's refused (status 422) if any of these is missing or blank, or if the date isn't a real date. A new item starts out unclaimed.
- **`GET /items`**: the full board, showing every item whether it has been claimed or not. Nothing is ever removed.
- **`GET /items/waiting`**: only the items still waiting for their owners.
- **`GET /items/{id}`**: look at one item. Returns "not found" (404) if the number doesn't exist.
- **`POST /items/{id}/claim`**: send `owner_name` to mark the item as claimed and record who collected it.
  - Refused (409) if the item has already been claimed; the first owner's name stays.
  - Returns 404 if the item doesn't exist, and 422 if the name is blank.

You had no preference on two points, so I chose the simplest options:
- **Anyone using the board can mark an item as claimed.** There's no login or password.
- **The owner's name is visible to everyone** who looks at a claimed item.

If you'd rather limit claiming to desk staff or hide owners' names, either can be added later.
